blocks.text:
Our first stop is Fazenda Ponte Alta.

More than 500 enslaved people worked on this estate. The plantation was established by the Baron of Mambucaba, who chose this region for coffee farming.

During the visit, you will learn about the estate’s history and coffee production.

blocks.text:
Next, we travel to Fazenda Taquara.

The enslaved people who worked here named the farm after the abundance of slender bamboo on its grounds.

The main house is believed to have been built in the 1830s.

Lunch is planned after the tour and is **not included in the price**.

blocks.text:
In the afternoon, we visit Fazenda Florença.

This estate has operated as a coffee plantation since 1852.

After the tour, transfer to Visconde de Mauá.

Overnight at the hotel.
